newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to June 13.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to June 13.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 39.43 percent decline in its turnover during the week ending June 13, after sale of state T-bills began to lose momentum.
Total turnover fell to 35.139 million dinars in 144 deals from 59.018 million dinars in 164 transactions a week ago.
Primary market turnover stood at 32.039 million dinars, there was no secondary market activity, while 3.1 million dinars resulted from a sale of shares.

Traders said overall activity fell after the state sold fewer of its T-bills than in the previous week. Some said the market fell prey to pre-weekend reallocation of funds in order to pay out pensions to around 1.3 million Serbian pensioners.

"It was a dull week despite almost unchanged liquidity and practically nothing to influence activity. Everybody seems to be waiting for something to happen, but nobody seems to know exactly what. Industry activity is halted, there is no real life in this economy," a trader told Reuters.

He said market participants were looking forward to some action now that the 1.254 billion German marks raised from sale of 49 percent stake in the Telekom Srbija last week are deposited on Serbian banks accounts.
For the week ending June 13, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper accounted for 136 transactions totalling 17.569 million dinars.
* Treasury bills traded four times for a volume of 0.27 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between 6.00 and 16.75 percent per month, while maturity stood between seven and 30 days.
* The bourse reported two transactions in state T-bills totalling 14.1 million dinars.
* There was no activity in the central bank short-term bonds.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper and treasury bills rose to 36.432 million dinars from 32.926 million a week ago.
* OTC trade in giro-money, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, rose to 31.1 million dinars from 25.25 million in the previous week. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
